text:
jess: quick check — I'm seeing ambiguous behavior when a flag is set at route+canary and also at model scope. which wins? example: route /chat has canary=20% enabled, but model 'gpt-small-v2' has the flag off. we expected model-level to block for that model, but prod looked like the route canary still applied. anyone seen this?
sam: I think our intended rule was "most specific wins" but i can't remember whether model scoped settings were considered more specific than route-level canaries.
maria: fwiw we document scope order as org -> project -> route -> model in the old PR, but iirc the canary evaluation lived in the routing layer which checks route first. so that could explain it.
cheng: we should make the rule explicit and implement a single resolution order. proposal: evaluate scope specificity first (model > route > project > org). within each scope, evaluate audience/canary overrides (audience-specific flag true/false) before falling back to the scope default.
jess: that sounds reasonable. can you give a tiny pseudo impl so ops/devs know what to expect?
cheng: sure — quick sketch:

```
resolve_flag(request, flag):
  // 1) model-level audience check
  if model_scope := lookup(flag, scope=MODEL, model_id=request.model_id):
    if match_audience(model_scope, request): return model_scope.value
    if model_scope.has_default: return model_scope.default

  // 2) route-level audience check
  if route_scope := lookup(flag, scope=ROUTE, route_id=request.route):
    if match_audience(route_scope, request): return route_scope.value
    if route_scope.has_default: return route_scope.default

  // 3) project -> org fallbacks
  if project_scope := lookup(flag, scope=PROJECT, project_id=request.project):
    return project_scope.value_or_default
  return lookup(flag, scope=ORG).value_or_default
```

cheng: important: audience checks are scoped — e.g., a 20% route canary only applies when evaluating the route scope, and won't be applied to model scope entries.
maria: that matches what we need for model owners to opt-out of route canaries for specific models. good.
sam: 👍 for the rule. we should add a small unit test matrix for route vs model combos and a note in flags.md.
jess: who wants to own the docs + tests?
cheng: i'll add tests to flag-resolver suite and open a docs PR to flags.md with the exact precedence table. cc @maria for review.
maria: ack. i'll add a note about audit logs — we should also record "which scope resolved" in the flag trace so it’s easy to debug.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled to run flag-resolver unit tests in CI in 10m.
jess: thanks all — let's aim to merge tests + docs today. :thumbsup:
